skill.name: ui-design-system
skill.description: Design system toolkit for defining color, typography, spacing, sizing, border, shadow, animation, breakpoint, and z-index tokens from a brand color.
skill.summary: Create structured UI design tokens and export them for implementation.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All three static findings are false positives caused by ordinary design terminology and Markdown command formatting. No command execution, system reconnaissance, prompt injection, or other semantic security issue was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged line assigns the numeric value 8 to a spacing-grid configuration field. It performs no system inspection or reconnaissance.
The backticks are Markdown formatting around a documented Python command. SKILL.md does not execute Ruby, shell commands, or user-controlled input.
The phrase describes an 8-point spacing grid feature in documentation. It does not request or perform system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Teams often define interface values inconsistently across design and code. This skill structures reusable tokens from a brand color for clearer implementation handoff.
actual_capabilities: Defines primary, secondary, neutral, semantic, and surface color token groups.
Builds typography scales, font families, weights, line heights, letter spacing, and text styles.
Creates spacing, sizing, border, shadow, animation, breakpoint, and z-index token structures.
Formats generated token data as JSON or CSS custom properties.
Accepts a brand color and modern, classic, or playful style through command-line arguments.
limitations: The current script contains a malformed warning color literal, so it cannot run until that source line is corrected.
SCSS is advertised, but the script does not define the SCSS export method.
Accessibility claims are not supported by contrast calculations or automated checks.
Component documentation is described, but only token generation code is included.

use_cases.title: Establish a visual foundation
use_cases.description: Generate a structured starting point for colors, typography, spacing, elevation, and responsive values.
use_cases.target_user: UI designers starting a design system

use_cases.title: Align implementation values
use_cases.description: Translate shared design decisions into JSON or CSS token structures for frontend work.

use_cases.title: Audit token coverage
use_cases.description: Compare an existing token set with common categories and identify missing foundations or inconsistent naming.
use_cases.target_user: Design system leads maintaining shared standards

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic token plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a design token plan for [brand color] using the [modern, classic, or playful] style. Summarize colors, typography, spacing, and breakpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new interface

prompt_templates.title: Prepare implementation tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a token specification for [product type] using [brand color]. Include semantic colors, type scale, spacing, component sizes, borders, shadows, and breakpoints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Detailed handoff from design to development

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing system
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these existing design tokens: [paste token summary]. Identify missing categories, naming inconsistencies, accessibility concerns, and migration priorities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate audit of a current design system

prompt_templates.title: Plan a token migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a migration plan from [current system] to semantic design tokens. Map legacy values, define aliases, handle themes, and propose staged validation.

output_examples.input: Use brand color #2563EB with a modern style and summarize the token system.
output: Primary and complementary color scales with semantic status colors
Modern font families, modular type sizes, weights, line heights, and text styles
An 8-point spacing foundation with component sizing and responsive breakpoints
Border, shadow, animation, and layering values for implementation

output_examples.input: Prepare a playful token direction for a youth learning application.
output_examples.output: A playful direction with larger radii, expressive typography choices, semantic colors, motion timing, consistent spacing, and responsive layout thresholds.

output_examples.input: Audit a product token set that only contains colors and spacing.
output_examples.output: The review identifies missing typography, sizing, borders, elevation, motion, breakpoints, and layering tokens, then prioritizes additions for developer handoff.

best_practices: Validate the brand color and style inputs before generating tokens.
Review contrast, focus states, and semantic meanings with accessibility tools before release.
Adopt semantic aliases and document token ownership before integrating generated values.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated values as approved production standards without design and engineering review.
Do not create duplicate tokens for identical meanings across separate components.
Do not rely on color alone to communicate status or interaction state.

faq.question: Which output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The code implements JSON and CSS output. SCSS is listed in documentation, but its export method is currently missing.

faq.question: Which visual styles are available?
faq.answer: The generator includes modern, classic, and playful presets for typography, border radius, and shadows.

faq.question: Can I use a custom brand color?
faq.answer: Yes. The command accepts a six-digit hexadecimal brand color and builds primary and complementary scales from it.

faq.question: Does this skill verify accessibility?
faq.answer: No. It provides semantic colors, but it does not calculate contrast ratios or run accessibility tests.

faq.question: Does the script require third-party packages?
faq.answer: No. It imports only Python standard library modules.

faq.question: Is the generated system ready for production?
faq.answer: Not immediately. Correct the current source defects, validate generated values, test accessibility, and align naming with your implementation architecture.
